findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility during food operations. The inspector recommends more employees getting the certification. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the interior of the ice machine has an accumulation of soil residues. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 1/20/2026 to ensure that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a buildup of frost on the reach-in freezers. The freezers must be defrosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. The grease and food residue on the floor to the right of the fryers. The inspector and PIC discussed installing a barrier (such as metal or plastic) between the fryer and wall to avoid debris accumulation on the floor.

(2) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The grease and dust on the white selves around the triple sink (especially near the fryers).

(3) The dust on the top of the magnetic knife strip.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no one present at the facility has an allergen awareness certificate. The inspector recommends more employees getting the certification. Ensure there is someone present at the facility with an allergen awareness certificate at the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 55-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: shredded cheese 56F, colby jack cheese 55F, mozzarella cheese 55F, cheese slices 54F, cream cheese x3 50-54F, sour cream 53F, ground beef 57F, mayo 55F, salami 58F, sausage 49F, beef 55F, cooked vegetables 55F, ham x3 55-50F, ranch 56F, cheese sauce 55F, and cheddar cheese 58F. All foods has been inside the cooler for over four hours. During the inspection all temperature control for safety (TCS) were voluntary discarded by the PIC (the above mentioned were the TCS foods discarded). There was a package of sausage, steak, and multiple pizzas that were recently purchased that had temperatures below 41F; these were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. The non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. unopened ranch, unopened mayo, uncut tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce in the harvest cut, and bread). The PIC was instructed that they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holing foods at 41F or below. The inspector suggests immediate service for the cooler. The inspector will follow-up on 7/14/2025 to check that the cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the mop was stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The employee working in the kitchen was informed and they hung the mop during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to airdry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a can of butane fuel stored on a top shelf above various foods (including, but not limited too, seasoning, sauces, maple syrup, icing, sugar, and flour). The butane fuel was removed from the location and moved to the dry storage area. Ensure that chemicals are always stored separate from food.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service -and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand washing sink was blocked when the inspector arrived. The items blocking the sink were removed during the inspection. Ensure hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times for employee use.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the top right side of the prep cooler had an ambient air temperature between 47F and 51F. A head of lettuce was probed to be 47F. The foods being kept in the top right portion of the cooler were mostly non-TCS (temperature control for safety) foods. Foods in the cooler that are TCS were moved to the bottom of the cooler which was temping at 41F or below during the inspection (including, but not limited too, yum yum sauce and ranch). Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less. For information about the coolers see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS foods without date marking. Food without date marking included, but is not limited too, the entire top left side of the prep cooler (this included cut vegetables such as carrots, peppers, and onions), wasabi in the sushi prep cooler, shrimp in the sushi prep cooler, spicy tuna in the sushi prep cooler, bowl of cheese in the double cooler, bowl of cut veggies in the double cooler, bowl of rice in the double cooler, and half & half at the bar. The PIC was confident when all the foods were prepped so date marks were added to all the above mentioned foods. Ensure that TCS foods held in the facility for longer that 24 hours are date marked to clearly indicate the 7-day maximum. The day the food was prepped is day 1. After 7 days the food must be discarded.

There was also an incorrect date mark on the avocados in the prep cooler. The date was 08/25/2024 (which would mean the food needed to be discarded), but the PIC stated the avocados were prepped yesterday. It appears that an employee is not removing dates from containers when they are emptied. Old date marks must be removed and new dates be added. Ensure foods are date marked with the correct dates.

The inspector will return on 09/16/2024 to check on date marking.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the top right of the prep cooler was not holding temperatures at 41F or below. The rest of the cooler was functioning correctly. The inspector will return on 09/16/2024 to ensure the cooler is functioning properly, or that there is not any TCS foods being stored in this portion of the cooler. For information about the foods see violation #22.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The fryer area needs cleaned. The sides of the grill and the wall on the other side of the fryer, as well as behind the fryer are soiled in a thick layer of grease. Use degreaser and soap/water/sanitizer to clean. Establish a routine cleaning schedule. Facility does a significant amount of frying and this area should be addressed. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.
2. The toaster oven above the prep cooler as you enter the kitchen is soiled with food splash and debris. Ensure the inside of the toaster oven is routinely cleaned. Oven grates are covered in foil and changed nightly, per PIC. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.
3. The oven below the grill is soiled with a thick layer of black, burnt food debris. Routinely clean the oven. Utilizes a oven cleaning agent if need be to appropriately clean the oven and scrub. The oven needs cleaning as needed. THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.
4. The white shelves holding clean dishes over the kitchen triple sink have an accumulation of dust and soil. Ensure that shelves are cleaned on a regular basis to protect clean dishes from contamination. 
5. The holder of the bar soda dispenser had an accumulation of mold. The PIC removed the holder from service and cleaned it in the dish machine during the inspection. Ensure the soda dispenser remains clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED ON SITE.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean the above areas as needed to prevent debris, food splash, and grease. Clean by the next routine inspection.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

(REPEAT) Observed several items in the bottom prep cooler and reach-in cooler that lacked date marking. Items were made the night before per PIC. Ensure staff is aware to adhere to a 7-day date marking system. Items were dated (shrimp tempura, seaweed salad, defrosted fish). COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 10/31/23. Staff should be diligent with date marking of foods. Discard within 7 days of the day prepared and/or opened.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink at the sushi station had a sanitizer bucket and hand soap sitting in the sink. Having items in the sink, even if they are items used for cleaning/sanitizing or used in the process of hand washing, must remain OUTSIDE the sink at all times to facilitate easy access to the hand sink. Employees should not have to touch ANYTHING in order to wash hands in any of the designated hand sinks at the facility. Operator expressed concern that there is limited space in this area. Consider a rack or other means of storage to put items on in this area to declutter and allow for appropriate storage. Ensure that hand sinks remain accessible at ALL times of operations. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The ice machine in the kitchen has a large amount of mold accumulation along the right wall, the upper edge of the baffle above ice tray, and along the seals along the rear access of the machine. All ice made in and contained in the ice machine is being discarded immediately. The ice bin and ice machine must be cleaned and sanitize before use. The ice bin at the bar has been cleaned and sanitized during the inspection and ice was purchased at an approved facility to allow ice to be used throughout the shift. Corrected on site - no further follow-up required. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Four sanitizer buckets and the third triple sink basin in the kitchen were filled with sanitizer solution lower than the required concentration for quaternary ammonium applications. All concentrations were approximately 50-100 ppm quaternary ammonium. Additional tablets of sanitizer were added to all basins to allow for proper sanitizing. Corrected on site. No further follow-up required. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
er Food Code as adopted, any foods exceeding time and/or temeprature criteria must be discarded. Several containers of prepared and/or TCS foods in the reach-in portion of the prep-cooler are observed to have date markings exceding the seven day requirements. These foods must be discarded immediately. Ensure that date marking is occurring on all prepared items and TCS items which have been opended and that if date marked, the date mark correctly corresponds to the date prepared/opened to easily identify items that must be discarded. Items discarded during this inspection include but are not limited to cheese sauce, noodles, and other prepared items. Staff states that some of the items were made within the past 7 days. Inspector explained that the date mark is considered the official record of when the foods were prepared and/or opened and indicates the safe timeframe during which foods may be prepared for service. Inspetor stressed the importance of proper training regarding date marking for new staff as well. A follow-up is being issued for date marking on November 3, 2023. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
A bright green wiping cloth was observed sitting on the counter. The wiping cloth was wet. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution when not actively being used or wiping surfaces to prevent microbial growth in the cloth itself. Dry wiping cloths may be stored on counters and other surfaces. Ensure that all wiping cloths are stored properly during the next routine inspection. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM THE PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S) (PO).

The counter along the north half-wall of the bar with exposed raw wood is still present from the pre-opening inspection. Raw wood is an absorbent surface and is not allowed in areas subject to food/moisture unless sealed against the intrusion of such food and/or moisture. During the pre-opening, the counter was discussed and replacement was planned. Ensure that all surfaces in areas subject to food/moisture are SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
